status_note: personal derivative of mendableai/open-lovable (Firecrawl); not a GitHub fork; adds a Crawl4AI FastAPI microservice + Docker; commits .omc/ agent-state files and __pycache__; single contributor
core_problem: Clone or re-imagine an existing website: scrape a URL to markdown + screenshot, hand it to an LLM that emits a full Vite/React project as <file> tags, write those files into a remote sandbox (E2B or Vercel Sandbox) running Vite, and iterate with targeted edits.
architecture: Next.js app router with ~25 API routes under app/api/*. The fork's own delta (CHANGES.md) is small: five routes that called Firecrawl now call crawl4ai-service/main.py, a 165-line FastAPI wrapper exposing GET /scrape (AsyncWebCrawler with BrowserConfig(enable_stealth) + CrawlerRunConfig(magic=True, wait_until=networkidle, delay_before_return_html=3.0), returns {markdown}) and GET /screenshot (base64 PNG); optional residential proxy and a commented-out CapSolver Turnstile solver. /api/search is stubbed to [] and /api/extract-brand-styles now returns raw markdown because Firecrawl's branding format has no equivalent. Upstream architecture retained: app/api/scrape-url-enhanced/route.ts fetches markdown+screenshot in parallel, sanitizes smart quotes and returns {content, screenshot, structured}. app/api/generate-ai-code-stream/route.ts (2k lines) is a single streaming Vercel AI SDK call: builds a ~400-line system prompt of shouted rules ('CRITICAL RULE - VIOLATION WILL RESULT IN FAILURE'), appends conversation context from global.conversationState (scraped websites, recently created files 'DO NOT RECREATE'), for edits fetches sandbox files, builds a FileManifest (types/file-manifest.ts: FileInfo with imports/exports/componentInfo, routes, componentTree) via lib/file-parser.ts regexes, classifies the prompt with lib/edit-intent-analyzer.ts (regex table -> EditType UPDATE_COMPONENT/ADD_FEATURE/FIX_ISSUE/REFACTOR/FULL_REBUILD/UPDATE_STYLE/ADD_DEPENDENCY plus a fileResolver per type) and lib/context-selector.ts (primary files to edit + App/tailwind/index.css/package.json always in context), then asks for complete files in <file path="...">...</file> tags (or <edit> blocks when MORPH_API_KEY enables lib/morph-fast-apply.ts). app/api/apply-ai-code-stream/route.ts parseAIResponse() regex-extracts <file>, <package(s)>, <command> tags, normalizes paths under /home/user/app/src, writes via the SandboxProvider abstraction (lib/sandbox/types.ts abstract class with e2b-provider.ts / vercel-provider.ts; factory.ts picks by env) and installs detected packages. lib/build-validator.ts validateBuild() waits 3 s, fetches the sandbox URL, and decides success by string checks (not the default Vite page, contains id="root", no 'vite-error-overlay'); classifyError() maps messages to missing-package/syntax/timeout/not-rendered and calculateRetryDelay() picks backoff. State is process-global (global.activeSandbox, global.conversationState, global.sandboxState: ~66 references across three routes), i.e. single-tenant. app/generation/page.tsx (4.1k lines) orchestrates the UI: scrape-screenshot -> extract-brand-styles -> scrape-url-enhanced -> generate-ai-code-stream -> apply-ai-code-stream -> sandbox iframe, plus inject-inspector for click-to-select.
core_innovation: Nothing new in the fork itself; upstream's idea is a FileManifest + regex edit-intent classifier that narrows an LLM edit to predicted target files, with generated code exchanged as <file> tags and validated by probing the live Vite sandbox.
strengths: SandboxProvider abstract class (createSandbox/runCommand/writeFile/readFile/listFiles/installPackages/getSandboxUrl/terminate) cleanly separates E2B from Vercel Sandbox behind one interface.
FileManifest data model (imports/exports/componentInfo/routes/componentTree/styleFiles) is a reasonable minimal project index for targeted edits, and EditIntent carries confidence + suggestedContext.
The Crawl4AI service keeps a stable {markdown} contract so callers did not change; docker-compose wires health checks between the two containers.
build-validator's error taxonomy (missing-package, syntax-error, sandbox-timeout, not-rendered, vite-error) with per-type retry delays is a small, reusable classification.
extractMissingPackages() parses three import-failure message shapes and feeds auto-install: a concrete self-heal loop.
weaknesses: The fork adds almost nothing architecturally; it degrades upstream (search stubbed, brand extraction reduced to raw markdown) and commits tool state (.omc/, __pycache__, .replit-tasks).

Website-cloning is the pipeline the architect already rejected for V1; the Cloudflare/anti-bot bypass layers (stealth driver, residential proxy, CAPTCHA solving) are a legal and ethical liability for an agency product.

Generation is one streaming shot with a prompt built from shouted imperatives and emoji; there is no plan, no schema, no structured output; correctness relies on regex-parsing <file> tags from free text.
Validation is string-sniffing the sandbox HTML after a fixed 3 s sleep (no 'vite-error-overlay', has id=root); no axe, Lighthouse, or runtime execution checks.
Process-global mutable state (global.activeSandbox etc.) makes it single-user by construction; 4.1k-line page component and 2k-line route file.
Regex file parser and regex intent classifier are brittle (upstream comments admit fallbacks); brand extraction is now 'the AI can infer brand styles from markdown'.
1 star, one contributor, last push May 2026; upstream mendableai/open-lovable is the maintained lineage.
patterns_to_steal: Error taxonomy + per-class retry policy (classifyError/calculateRetryDelay) -> QA/fix loop: classify Playwright/Lighthouse/axe failures into fixed categories with distinct retry or escalation rules.

Provider abstraction for the execution environment (SandboxProvider abstract class) -> agent orchestration: one interface for local build vs remote preview runner so Astro builds can run in CI, locally, or a sandbox without touching the pipeline.

Edit-intent -> target-file narrowing (FileManifest + EditIntent.targetFiles/suggestedContext) -> post-V1 visual editor and fix loop: map a fix request to the specific SiteDefinition sections and design tokens it may touch, and pass only those to the model.
Scrape contract {markdown, screenshot} with quote sanitization -> research stage only as an input to the FactRegistry (owner-supplied URLs), never as a design corpus.
patterns_to_avoid: Crawl -> screenshot -> 'clone this site' generation -> rejected website-cloner pipeline; trade-dress and copyright exposure.
Cloudflare bypass / residential proxy / CAPTCHA solving -> not acceptable for an agency product; if we crawl, we crawl owner-authorized sources politely.
Free-text <file> tag output parsed by regex -> our model output is Zod-validated JSON selections, never source code.
Prompt engineering by shouting (dozens of 'CRITICAL ... VIOLATION = FAILURE' lines) -> replace with schema constraints and deterministic gates.
Validation by sniffing HTML strings after a sleep -> use real Playwright crawl + axe + Lighthouse budgets.
Process-global state for sandbox/conversation -> pipeline state must be persisted per job (Postgres) and snapshotted.
reusable_patterns: ErrorClassRetryPolicy: map failure messages to a small enum and attach a distinct backoff/escalation per class.
IntentToTargetNarrowing: classify an edit request and resolve it to the minimal set of artefacts the model may modify.
StableScrapeContract: swap scraping backends behind a fixed {markdown, screenshot} shape.
adoption_strategy: Ignore. The fork's contribution is a thin Crawl4AI wrapper plus anti-bot bypasses on top of a cloning pipeline the architect has already excluded; its generation and validation are weaker than OpenThorn's and structurally incompatible with a typed SiteDefinition. The only things worth keeping are two small generalizable patterns (error-class retry policy, execution-provider interface), which we can write from scratch in an afternoon. If crawling is ever needed for FactRegistry ingestion, evaluate upstream Crawl4AI directly (Tier-1 elsewhere), not this wrapper.
